correctness.rationale: The frozen theorem survives, but its proof at RESULT.md line 28 gives the wrong leading coefficient for P T_b−Q T_a: only one derivative occurs in either term, so the coefficient is (a−b)2^{a+b−2}, not ab(a−b)2^{a+b−2}. For (a,b)=(2,3), direct expansion gives −8t^4+6t^2−3, not leading coefficient −48. The explicit corrected proof and coefficient regression are delivered under repairs/5. The base-point-free original map is birational since its generic degree divides both a and b; pullback degree b and Chebyshev composition identify its image with the asserted equation. P and Q have disjoint simple roots, so the corrected Gauss coordinates have no common zero; characteristic-zero biduality gives dual degree a+b−1. For W=P Q'−Q P', the differentiated ODE gives (1−t^2)W'=3tW−(b^2−a^2)PQ. W is nonzero at ±1 by this identity and at zeros of P,Q by their simplicity and disjointness. Thus every root of the degree-(a+b−3) Wronskian is simple, including complex roots. The vanishing sequence (0,b−a,b) gives the infinity weight. The dual normalization has only the infinite parameter over [1:0:0]; the orders a,b there are coprime and yield precisely the asserted Puiseux pair and delta. At every finite W root the graph second derivative W/P^3 has a simple zero, so the slope/intercept orders are 2,3, giving a cuspidal branch, not necessarily a distinct dual point. Inspected the frozen report and checker without executing them. Replayed the corrected exact checker with SymPy via python /workspace/repairs/5/verify_chebyshev_dual.py; all 73 bounded pairs passed, now including the coefficient that the frozen script never tested.
